### Step 1 — Scene
A small snack or dessert plate with a whole apple, four tan rectangular pieces, and a chocolate-drizzled pastry or wafer bar. The tan pieces are ambiguous; I’m estimating them as **peanut-butter-style fudge**.

### Step 2 — Vessel
Likely a **26 cm dinner plate**.  
Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ **531 cm²**.

### Steps 3–7 — Items, area, volume, weight, and energy
Heights are average heights across each footprint, accounting for the apple’s rounded shape. Bulk densities provide the only volume-to-weight reduction.

| Visible item | Plate area covered | Area | Average height | Gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Whole red apple | 11% | 58 cm² | 4.3 cm | 249 ml | 0.8 g/ml | 199 g | 52 | 103 kcal |
| Four tan pieces, assumed peanut-butter fudge | 6% | 32 cm² | 2.5 cm | 80 ml | 1.0 g/ml | 80 g | 450 | 360 kcal |
| Pastry/wafer bar, including chocolate drizzle | 7% | 37 cm² | 1.3 cm | 48 ml | 0.55 g/ml | 26 g | 480 | 125 kcal |

The food footprints total **24% of the plate**, consistent with the substantial empty space. No separate oil or dressing is visible; the chocolate is included in the bar estimate.

### Step 8 — Sanity check
The estimated **305 g and 588 kcal** are plausible for an apple and two small, energy-dense sweets. The greatest uncertainty is the identity of the tan pieces: if they are tofu rather than fudge, the energy would be substantially lower.
